claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr state is an equiatomic, single-phase BCC random solid solution with minimal short-range order.
Hybrid MC/MD can evolve an initially random BCC configuration and reveal thermally driven nanostructural or chemical-order evolution.
Periodically re-randomizing atomic configurations suppresses SRO formation while otherwise providing a valid disordered control.
Elevated temperature induces short-range ordering or local atomic clustering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Increasing temperature enhances atomic mobility and thereby promotes SRO-cluster formation.
SRO or clustering locally distorts the lattice.
SRO clusters act as effective obstacles to dislocation glide and enhance dislocation pinning.
SRO-mediated dislocation pinning produces anomalous retention or a plateau in yield strength as temperature increases.
Locally ordered regions modify interatomic bonding.
The elastic modulus will not decrease monotonically with temperature and may plateau or behave anomalously.
The yield strength will not decrease monotonically with temperature and may plateau or behave anomalously.
SRO-induced lattice stiffening lowers the thermal expansion coefficient relative to a disordered state.
The proposed mechanism operates from approximately 300 K to 1473 K, provided phase transitions and complete cluster disordering do not occur.
A fully disordered state is expected to show traditional thermal-softening trends in yield strength, elastic modulus, and thermal response.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify temperature-matched re-randomized configurations as the control, whereas the predicted outcome is framed relative to a room-temperature disordered baseline. These are different comparisons and could confound SRO effects with ordinary temperature effects.
